themes_detail.label: Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting a localized environmental hazard or industrial emission event requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 3 air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme deviation
No prior pattern of air quality complaints in district suggests acute event
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP and EPA to determine source—industrial facility, construction, or weather pattern?
Interview residents in Coney Island/Brighton Beach about respiratory symptoms or visible pollution
Cross-reference with any new construction permits or industrial activity filed in last 2 weeks

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69), suggesting either a crackdown by city agencies or emerging illegal vending operations in the district.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
No prior vendor enforcement pattern suggests new enforcement activity or emerging illegal vending
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD and DOE to determine if new vendor enforcement operation is underway
Identify specific locations and types of vendors being cited—street food, merchandise, unlicensed services?
Interview local vendors and business improvement districts about impact

themes_detail.label: Street Obstructions Blocking Access
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints surged to 6 THIS WEEK, up from a baseline of 0.5 per week (1100% increase, z-score: 7.78), indicating sidewalk, curb, or pedestrian access blockages requiring immediate public space clearance.
evidence: 6 obstruction complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 7.78 indicates extreme statistical deviation
Pattern aligns with overgrown tree/branches spike (3 complaints this week) suggesting environmental cause
reporting_angles: Map the 6 obstruction complaints geographically to identify if concentrated in one neighborhood
Determine if obstructions stem from construction, fallen trees, vendor encroachment, or parked vehicles
Check if related to overgrown vegetation spike (also hitting this week)

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees & Branches Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about overgrown trees and branches jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.2 per week (1100% increase, z-score: 6.35), potentially creating pedestrian hazards and sight-line obstructions on residential streets and parks.
evidence: 3 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates statistically significant spike
Converges with street obstruction spike (6 complaints this week) and missing street sign complaints (4 last week)
reporting_angles: Identify specific parks or streets where trees are overgrown—Seaside Park, residential avenues?
Contact NYC Parks to determine if maintenance backlog or storm damage is responsible
Check if recent weather events (wind, rain) caused branch damage or if this reflects under-pruning

themes_detail.label: Street Signage Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints (damaged and missing combined) totaled 7 over the past 2 weeks (3 damaged 3 weeks ago, 4 missing last week), up 700% from baseline, indicating possible systematic wayfinding failure or recent vandalism wave affecting traffic safety.
evidence: 4 missing street sign complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 4.95)
3 damaged street sign complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Combined 7 sign complaints over 2 weeks suggests either maintenance gap or coordinated vandalism
reporting_angles: Request DOT data on street sign replacement and repair backlogs in CD313
Canvass the district to identify missing/damaged signs—are they concentrated in specific areas?
Determine if damage pattern matches vandalism reports or reflects deferred maintenance
